newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures posted their largest one-day gain since September 13 to hit their highest level this year on weak German economic data and relief Russian President Yeltsin's heart operation appeared successful.

The December contract got its initial boost from a surprise drop in September German industrial orders which analysts said helped allay some concerns about German rate rises even though the numbers are often volatile.
Analysts said U.S. bonds, buoyed by polls which suggested the Republicans would hold Congress, had helped boost French bonds, driving the benchmark 10-yield down to 5.89 percent.
"The much weaker-than-expected German numbers were a helpful factor," said Sean Shepley, international economist at CS First Boston.
"The political pressure for lower rates is still very strong. There's no upward momentum in the French economy, and arguably it's the same in Germany."

The December bond future surged through resistance at 126.60, triggering stop losses, after the news that Yeltsin's operation had been successful. The contract baulked initially at 126.80, the previous high, before getting another lift from Bunds to reach 127.00.
Further strength in the United States then pushed it to a session high of 127.04. After the Matif close the contract passed resistance at 127.12/14 in the GLOBEX session to reach 127.24.
A trader said, "the most important thing was to have closed above 126.80, as otherwise one could have had the impression of a false breakout (of the recent range)."
The contract has been stuck in a range between 125.60 and 126.80 for the past month.
The trader said he had revised his forecast for the end of the year to 130 from 127-128.
Traders said there was little buying in the cash market given the sharp drop in yields, which could prompt some caution on the part of primary dealers ahead of Thursday's OAT auction.

As expected, the Treasury said on Tuesday it would be selling the benchmark 6.50 percent 2006 OAT, the TEC 10 variable rate OAT and the 8.25 percent 2004 OAT, currently the cheapest to deliver for the December futures contract.

One trader said although it was not the most propitious time to place paper, the TEC would always find demand and the 2004 needed to be sold now so the payment date would be before the date for final delivery of the bonds at the futures expiry.

December PIBOR climbed slightly but failed to break through the contract high reached last week at 96.49. The back months outperformed strongly, pulled higher by Euromarks, although analysts said the lack of liquidity amplified the price swings.
The franc suffered early in the day to hit a low of 3.3857 before a dollar rally against the mark pushed the French unit back above 3.3800 to a high of 3.3773.
Market sources also said French welfare debt repayment fund CADES was planning to tap its three existing franc bonds, 2002, 2005 and 2007, next Wednesday and had asked for comments on its proposal.
